title: No field, column or element exists for the subrogation position or for the guaranteed amount that R-GUA-22 compares the payment with
source: _work/msr/context/S3.md (ownership rows of S3); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v2.md (T3.1, T3.2, T4); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3.md (A2.4.3.1, A2.4.4.1); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-016 Data, Screen and states); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md (R-GUA-22, R-GUA-23, R-GUA-24); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R9)
section: CON s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 3 and 5; s8 BR2 and BR4; s11 Data; s12.1 REST operations provided; s12.7 Tables owned; s12.8 Contract fakes; s13; s15; s16 C2 and C7. APP s3; s4 Flow step 5; s7 Acceptance criteria; s8 BR2 and BR7; s11 Data; s12.1; s15
description: AC3 asks the Workbench to record the TCG share against the case for all future recoveries, and R-GUA-22 compares claim_amount_paid with guaranteed_amount, but no source publishes a field for either value. The claim table of the service closes at eight fields, DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-022 (id, case_id, claim_type, claim_deadline, claimed_amount, filed_at, paid_amount, status), the legacy Data table of the key lists the same eight and says 'and 2 more' for that range, and the ownership rows give S3 that one table only. The position, its basis, its effective scope, its set-at time and the guaranteed amount therefore have no field ID, no column and no closed list, and SCR-17's five states carry no separate state for the position. The baseline declares the position and the guaranteed amount as elements of the claim answer and of the local decision record, adds no column and no table of its own making, and the data owner must name the field before a column arrives with the DB story of this service.
evidence: TSD S3 T3.1 declares guarantee_claim with DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-022 and no share, no basis, no guaranteed amount and no set-at field; T3.2 gives LOV-CLAIM-STATUS as PREPARING, FILED, DEFECT, PAID, REJECTED and LOV-CLAIM-TYPE with no share list; the legacy Data table of RWB-E4-016 lists guarantee_claim with 'id, case_id, claim_type, claim_deadline, claimed_amount, filed_at and 2 more' under DF-TRT-015 to DF-TRT-022; the legacy Screen and states row gives SCR-17 the five states Not due, due, submitted, paid, refused; the ownership rows of the context pack list one table, guarantee_claim, and no other store.
area: Data model and contract, S3 rwb-guarantee
owner_role: S3 rwb-guarantee service owner with the data steward and the P7 rwb-decision owner
proposed: The data owner names the field for the share, its basis, its effective scope and the guaranteed amount, and the DB story of this service adds the column in its own Flyway sequence; the contract then gains the elements in a minor version and no criterion, step or test changes.

title: The posted payment reaches this service only on an rwb-payment event, and the legacy v_ace_payment read is closed to it
source: _work/msr/context/S3.md (ownership rows of S3 and the Architecture v5 slide 13 connection matrix); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3.md (A2.4.2, A2.4.3.1); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v2.md (T5.2, T5.3); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-016 AC2, Data); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md (R-GUA-22); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R5.5 DP-05)
section: CON s3 Preconditions; s8 BR2 and BR5; s11 Data; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.4 Events consumed; s12.8 Contract fakes; s12.9. APP s2; s3; s4 Flow steps 2 and 3; s7 Acceptance criteria; s8 BR3 and BR8; s11 Data; s12.4; s12.8
description: AC2 asks the module to match the payment, post it and set the subrogation position, and the legacy Data table reads v_ace_payment (DF-ACE-043 to DF-ACE-054) on a direct connection. In the target the posting belongs to rwb-payment (P8), Arch v5 slide 8 states that the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views are read only by rwb-source-data, and the connection matrix of slide 13 gives S3 no REST edge at all and one event subscription from P8. The payment fact therefore arrives as an event, its name, its key and its element set are not published by any source, and this service holds no v_ace_payment grant. The step matches the event to the claim and posts nothing.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 13, row S3 Guarantee: the P7 cell is T, the P6 cell is T E, the P8 cell is E, and every other cell is empty; the same slide states that route services reach shared capabilities through Temporal, never REST; slide 8 states that the 30 recovery.v_ace_* views are read only by rwb-source-data; the legacy Data table of RWB-E4-016 lists v_ace_payment under DF-ACE-043 to DF-ACE-054; TSD S3 T5.3 gives the Events row as None and T5.2 lists only the published Java interfaces of P3, P7, P4, P5 and P6.
owner_role: P8 rwb-payment owner with the P1 rwb-source-data owner and the S3 service owner
proposed: The rwb-payment owner publishes the posted-payment event with its name, its key and its elements, and the fake is replaced by the published contract in a minor version; if a payment read turns out to be needed, it is published by rwb-payment and never read from an ACE view.

title: The service publishes no event, while the connection matrix shows three peers subscribing to it, and no peer event name is published
source: _work/msr/context/S3.md (ownership rows of S3 and the Architecture v5 slide 13 connection matrix); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v2.md (T5.3); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Event and Messaging Design v4.md; 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R4, R5.5 DP-09 and DP-14)
section: CON s3; s8 BR2 and BR6; s11 Data; s12.3 Events published; s12.4 Events consumed; s12.9. APP s2; s3; s8 BR9; s12.3; s12.4; s12.9
description: The ownership rows give rwb-guarantee zero events, so this story publishes nothing and the topic rwb.guarantee.events.v1 exists only under the naming rule. The connection matrix of slide 13 nevertheless shows P3 Case calling S3 through Temporal and events, P6 Comms through Temporal and events, and P9 Reporting listening to S3 events, and this service listening to P8 events. No source publishes an event name for the guarantee stage, and the payment event name is not published either, so the consumption row carries the placeholder and no name is invented.
evidence: The ownership rows of the context pack give S3 Events (0) and Jobs (0); Architecture v5 slide 13 gives the S3 column P3 cell T E, P6 cell T E and P9 cell E, and the S3 row P8 cell E; TSD S3 T5.3 names no event; Template and Rules v1 R4 fixes the topic as rwb.<short>.events.v1 and the event name as rwb.<short>.<Event>.v1.
owner_role: P9 rwb-reporting owner, P3 rwb-case owner and P6 rwb-comms owner with the S3 service owner
proposed: The event owner confirms the guarantee events the peers subscribe to and their names, and a later story adds them to rwb.guarantee.events.v1 with their outbox rows; the payment event name is confirmed by its owner and the placeholder is replaced in a minor version.

title: R-GUA-23 and R-GUA-24 carry the same action and differ only in their from-state, and the claim status list is not mapped to the GUARANTEE case states
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md (R-GUA-22, R-GUA-23, R-GUA-24); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v2.md (T3.2, T4); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3.md (A2.4.3.1); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-016 AC2, AC3)
section: CON s3; s8 BR1; s9; s16 C7. APP s3; s4 Flow step 4; s8 BR1; s9; s15; s16 TC-E4-016-02 and -03
description: Two rule rows carry the same event, the same condition, the same action and the same to-state and differ only in their from-state: R-GUA-23 leaves CLAIM_PAID and R-GUA-24 leaves CLAIM_PART_PAID. The legacy key carries only the CLAIM_PAID path in AC3, while FSD A2.4.3.1 lists both rows, so the partially paid claim is in the requirement but not in the criterion. Separately, the claim record carries the closed list LOV-CLAIM-STATUS (PREPARING, FILED, DEFECT, PAID, REJECTED) while the workflow carries seventeen GUARANTEE states (CLAIM_SUBMITTED, CLAIM_PAID, CLAIM_PART_PAID, SUBROGATION_POSITION and the rest), and no source maps one list to the other, so the record's PAID value and the case's CLAIM_PAID state are one step declared by this story and not a published mapping.
evidence: Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 lists R-GUA-23 as CLAIM_PAID, SUBROGATION_DUE, 'TCG holds a share of every later recovery' and R-GUA-24 as CLAIM_PART_PAID, SUBROGATION_DUE, with the same action and the same to-state SUBROGATION_POSITION; FSD S3 A2.4.3.1 lists both rows with identical rule text; TSD S3 T4 maps R-GUA-23 from CLAIM_PAID and R-GUA-24 from CLAIM_PART_PAID and T3.2 gives LOV-CLAIM-STATUS as PREPARING, FILED, DEFECT, PAID, REJECTED; the legacy AC3 names the CLAIM_PAID path only.
area: Rules and state model, S3 rwb-guarantee
owner_role: P7 rwb-decision owner with the business owner of module S3
proposed: The rule owner confirms whether the partially paid claim carries the same position, and the data owner publishes the mapping of LOV-CLAIM-STATUS to the GUARANTEE case states; if the partial path is confirmed, one activity serves both rows with no criterion change, and if a mapping is published the record carries it as a coded value.

title: The TCG share has no published source and the TCG interface INT-29 is recorded as not available
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v2.md (T5.1, T6.1); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD S3 Guarantees and guarantors v3.md (A2.4.2, A2.4.3.1, A2.4.3.3); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-016 Permission checks, Validation and messages); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4.md (R-GUA-23, R-GUA-24); _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3.md (FEAT-GUA-04)
section: CON s3; s8 BR4 and BR9; s11 Data; s12.1; s12.9; s14. APP s3; s4 Flow step 5; s8 BR2; s10 Authority; s13 Configuration and reference data; s14
description: AC3 records the TCG share and R-GUA-23 and R-GUA-24 condition it on 'TCG holds a share of every later recovery', but no source publishes where the share comes from: TSD S3 T5.1 records INT-29, the Thai Credit Guarantee Corporation, as 'Not available today; entered and filed by the guarantee officer', with no operation, file or payload, and the FSD names ALS and GL and the Workbench as the systems of the feature. The share, its basis and its effective scope are therefore governed values entered or confirmed by a person on the claim update under right U, and no TCG interface, endpoint or file is called; the placeholder and the gap stay until an owner publishes a source.
evidence: TSD S3 T5.1 gives one row, INT-29 Thai Credit Guarantee Corporation, direction Both, approach 'Not available today; entered and filed by the guarantee officer'; FSD S3 A2.4.2 names the integration points ALS and GL and Workbench; the Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 row of FEAT-GUA-04 names 'Runs unattended' as the primary role with the systems ALS and GL and Workbench; the legacy Permission checks give Treatment and offer U to RW-CASEOWN, RW-RESTRUCT, RW-SPECIAL and RW-GUARANT and no right to an unattended identity.
area: Reference data and integration, S3 rwb-guarantee
owner_role: S3 rwb-guarantee service owner with the business owner of module S3 and the P8 rwb-payment owner
proposed: The business owner names the source of the TCG share, either a governed reference row with its version or a TCG interface published by rwb-integration, and the value is read on that source; the element set and the criteria do not change.
